body:
## Question

Which lightweight way of loading glTF models fits Ridgeline without a full 3D engine such as three.js?

Compare candidate libraries and a minimal in-house GLB parser on:
- Download size added to the library (raw and gzip).
- License and maintenance status.
- The glTF subset each supports: GLB versus separate files, embedded textures, materials, mesh quantization and Draco or Meshopt compression.
- Whether parsing can run without blocking the main thread.

Identify the smallest subset needed for typical freely available vehicle models (drone, tank, plane, boat) and what would be rejected. The answer feeds the ticket that chooses how Ridgeline draws and loads models.

Map: [Entity models and representation switching](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/issues/71)

comments.body:
## Resolution

Findings: [`.scratch/entity-models/research/gltf-loading.md` at cc6edca](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/blob/cc6edca4e273378a1a801ad4cddebd753e934cc9/.scratch/entity-models/research/gltf-loading.md) on branch `research/gltf-loading`.

**Answer**

- A small in-house GLB parser covering a narrow subset is about a fifth the gzip size of the smallest library path, and a tenth to a twentieth of full loaders. The libraries' extra weight goes to editing, writing, compression hooks, or decoders fetched from public CDNs.
- loaders.gl, glTF-Transform and meshoptimizer are MIT and actively released. gltf-loader-ts was last published in 2018. Draco (Apache-2.0) last published its npm decoder in January 2024.
- Every freely licensed vehicle sample tested loads with the small subset. Draco, meshopt and KTX2 are not needed for them.
- For every option, WebGL uploads run on the main thread. Parsing the subset took 0.3 to 30 ms per model in Node. `createImageBitmap` decodes textures in parallel. Any candidate could run in a worker, but Ridgeline has no worker today.
- This does not choose the approach. That remains for #75.

**Smallest viable subset**

Accepts:

- GLB v2 with one embedded BIN buffer.
- The default scene's node tree, flattened to static transforms.
- Triangle lists with `POSITION`, plus optional `NORMAL`, `TEXCOORD_0` and `COLOR_0`. Flat normals are computed when `NORMAL` is missing.
- All core component types, including normalized and strided data. This covers `KHR_mesh_quantization`.
- `KHR_texture_transform`, which quantized UVs need.
- Base color factor and texture, alpha mode, double-sided, emissive factor, and `KHR_materials_unlit`.
- Embedded PNG and JPEG images.
- Animations, cameras, lights and optional extensions are ignored.

Rejects, by name:

- Any other `extensionsRequired` entry: Draco, `EXT_`/`KHR_meshopt_compression`, `KHR_texture_basisu`, and required WebP or AVIF.
- `.gltf` with separate files, external buffers, and external images unless a resolver is supplied. Offline repackaging to GLB works.
- Skins, morph targets, sparse accessors, non-triangle modes, and base-color textures on TEXCOORD_1.

Results: accepted Cesium_Air (plane), CesiumDrone, Ingenuity, GroundVehicle, the milk truck, ToyCar and CarConcept, a quantized Duck, and 321 Kenney GLBs (boats, ships, cars, spacecraft). Rejected the Draco ferrari and the KTX2 balloon. The 168 textured Kenney GLBs reference an external PNG, so they need a resolver or offline repackaging.

**Sizes** (Vite 8.3.0 library build like Ridgeline's, Node gzip, bytes)

| Option | Raw | Gzip |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| In-house subset parser (throwaway estimate, parser only) | 6,491 | 2,710 |
| loaders.gl 4.5.2 GLB container only | 47,526 | 12,933 |
| glTF-Transform 4.5.1 core | 85,526 | 20,758 |
| loaders.gl 4.5.2 full GLTFLoader | 189,621 | 49,878 |
| meshopt decoder alone | 27,663 | 7,481 |
| Draco glTF decoder (separate files) | 251,049 | 75,248 |
| Ridgeline today, for scale | 23,155 | 7,476 |

**Unverified:**

- Browser timings.
- Drawn output and model orientation.
- A tank model.
- Licenses of three of the Cesium models.
- Marketplace exports.
- The production size of an in-house parser.
- Workers in a browser.

title: Choose a lightweight glTF loading approach
